title: Exchange an infinite sum and integral
promptMarkdown: For $x\in[0,1)$, set $s_N(x)=\sum_{k=1}^N x^{2k}$. Compute $\int_0^1\sum_{k\ge1}x^{2k}\,dx$ as an extended integral. Then replace $x^{2k}$ by $2^{-k}x^{2k}$ and show the resulting integral is finite. You need not evaluate the latter series in closed form.
hintLadder: Use increasing partial sums, not a formal termwise integration rule.
Compare the first numerical series to the harmonic series and the second to a geometric series.

criteria.criterion: Justifies both interchanges by positivity and monotonicity.
